info.title: PillDrops API
info.description: PillDrops-shaped REST API for disposable Firecracker microVM sandboxes: create, exec, files, pause/resume, preview, templates, keys, usage, and audit. This document covers the core /v1 surface; some operational endpoints are omitted.

get.description: Returns 200 whenever the process is up and routing. Checks no dependencies: use /readyz to decide whether to send traffic.
Verifies this node's datastore is reachable. 503 means stop routing traffic here; it does not mean restart the process.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Repeat with the same key to replay the original response instead of creating a duplicate.

get.summary: List sandboxes for the caller's org

post.description: A disk that outlives the sandbox it is attached to. Attach it at create with `volumes: [{id, path}]`. Firecracker nodes only.

501.description: This node's runtime cannot attach volumes.

200.description: The volume; `attached_to` names the sandbox holding it.

404.description: No such volume in the caller's org.

delete.summary: Delete a volume and its data

patch.summary: Rename, re-slug, move the public port or change the idle auto-pause
patch.description: Absent fields are left alone. `slug` must start with a lowercase letter and be unique across the platform (`8000-x`, `agent-x` and reserved labels such as `www` are refused); `''` releases it. `port` moves the preview to another port without a restart; on the docker runtime it must be 8000 or a port the template declares. `idle_timeout` follows the create policy: seconds, clamped to 30 s..24 h; -1 = never auto-pause; 0 = platform default.

slug.description: DNS label served at https://<slug>.<domain>/ and accepted wherever an id is; empty releases it.

port.description: Public app port for the preview URL.

idle_timeout.description: Idle auto-pause in seconds; -1 = never, 0 = platform default.

200.description: The updated sandbox (`url` when a port is published).

400.description: Bad name or slug grammar, or `port_not_published`: the docker runtime publishes 8000 and the template's declared ports only.

409.description: `slug_taken`: another live sandbox holds the slug.

get.description: Probes a fixed candidate list (3000, 3001, 4200, 5000, 5173, 8000, 8080, 8081, 8888, 9000, 9323) plus the sandbox's public port and reports which answer. Detection, not a registry.

post.description: Stop the sandbox's compute while keeping its memory, processes and open sockets resident on the node. A wake is milliseconds and the app never restarts, unlike a pause, which writes the memory to disk and frees it. Standby holds the node's RAM, so the sandbox keeps its slot and is still billed for memory; only vCPU-seconds stop. Any exec, file or preview request wakes it.

standby_ms.description: How long the freeze took; 0 when the sandbox was already on standby.

501.description: This node's runtime cannot freeze a sandbox in RAM.

paused_ms.description: How long the snapshot took; 0 when the sandbox was already paused.

resume_ms.description: How long the restore took; 0 when the sandbox was already running.

post.description: Copy a running or paused sandbox into a new one: disk, memory and every running process. A running parent stands still only while its memory is written and its disk is copied, then carries on; a paused parent stays paused. The child comes up running with its own id, URL and token, and is independent from that moment. Counted against the plan like a create.

timeout.description: Child hard TTL in seconds; 0 = node default, negative = persistent.

201.description: Forked. The create response shape plus parent_id, parent_state, source ("fork/<parent>"), boot_ms and parent_paused_ms.

post.description: Take a named save point of a running sandbox. On Firecracker this captures memory and disk with the guest stopped only for the writes, so the sandbox keeps running and comes back with the same processes; on Docker it is a filesystem commit and the container is never stopped. At most 10 per sandbox, deleted with it. Saving over an existing name replaces it atomically.

201.description: Saved: name, created_at, size_bytes, snapshot_kind ("memory" or "disk") and status.

get.description: A sandbox's save points and the per-sandbox maximum. A capture that was interrupted lists with status "building" and cannot be restored.

post.description: Roll the sandbox back to a save point: same id, URL, token and address, and every write made after the checkpoint is discarded. A memory checkpoint comes back with its processes and listening sockets still running, so the start command is not relaunched; a disk checkpoint has lost them and it is. A paused sandbox is woken first.

409.description: checkpoint_not_ready, or the sandbox is mid-transition.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Sandbox-relative path. Rejected if it contains a '..' segment.

post.summary: Build a custom image or a Firecracker template from a build context
post.description:
Builds from the request body (a tar or tar.gz build context containing a Dockerfile) and produces ONE of two artifacts, selected by `runtime`:

- **docker** (the default) — a Docker image tagged for the calling org. Launch it with `pilldrops sandbox create --image <tag>`.
- **firecracker** — a TEMPLATE: the same context converted to a bootable squashfs rootfs, with the platform's boot machinery injected. Launch it with `pilldrops sandbox create --template <template_id>`.

The two are not interchangeable, and a build is never relayed to a node of the other runtime: if the fleet has no healthy node of the requested runtime the answer is 503 naming what the fleet does have.

A Firecracker template build requires a container engine on the building node even though that node boots microVMs, because the rootfs is produced by exporting a built container image's filesystem. It also requires squashfs-tools and an envd binary on the node (PD_ENVD_PATH, default /opt/pilldrops/bin/envd); a missing prerequisite is a 400 naming it, checked before the build starts.

The build runs on ONE node and the result is then published to the fleet's shared artifact store, so any node can obtain it. It previously ran on every node in the fleet, serially, with a 20-minute timeout each.

The body is capped by MAX_BUILD_CONTEXT_BYTES (default 512 MiB) rather than by the generic request cap.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Image name. The tag becomes sf-<org>-<name>:latest, and the template id is that tag without its version suffix.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: Which runtime the result must be bootable on, which decides both the node the build lands on and the kind of artifact published. Omitted (the default) prefers a docker node and produces an image tarball, which is the behaviour every caller had before Firecracker template builds existed.

200.description: The build ran. Check `ok`: it is true only when the image was built AND, on a fleet of more than one node, published to the shared store. A build that succeeded but could not be published reports ok=false with the reason in publish.error, because the image would then exist on exactly one node while placement is free to schedule the sandbox anywhere.

503.description: No healthy node to build on, or no healthy node of the requested `runtime`. The message names the runtimes the fleet actually has.

get.description: Lists the builds of a template, newest first, with the id of the one that is ready to boot. For operators and the CLI; it is not how a node resolves a template on the create path. An operator key sees every org's builds, a customer key only its own org's. Served by the control plane.

ready_build_id.description: The newest build that may be booted, or empty when the template has no completed publish.

post.description: Uploads a template's root filesystem as the raw request body and publishes it: the data object, its block-map header and metadata.json are written to the fleet's shared artifact store, read back and verified, and only then is the build marked ready. A publish that is interrupted at any point leaves the build unready and unbootable — a build is never ready before its bytes are durable. Requires the operator key: publishing decides what every node in the fleet boots. Served by the control plane, which is the only tier whose database role may write the build index.

parameters.name: build_id
parameters.description: Identifier for this build; generated when omitted. Re-using an existing one is refused with 409.

parameters.name: kernel_version
parameters.description: Boot-compatibility triple, recorded in metadata.json and cached on the build row for scheduling.

503.description: No artifact store is configured (ORCHESTRATOR_ARTIFACT_DIR), or the build index is not reachable

get.summary: List API keys for the org
Usage + credit summary for the org
Name the caller: the principal kind and the org it acts for (control plane)
get.description: A sandbox's own token (pd_sb_…, delivered to /run/pilldrops/token in the guest) answers principal=sandbox with its sandbox_id; an API key answers principal=key; the fleet key answers principal=operator. Sandbox principals are admitted only to sandbox routes (their own sandbox; org-wide create/list/get/exec/files/fork/ports); every other route answers 403 with a body naming the principal kind.

sandbox_id.description: Present when principal is sandbox: the sandbox the token was minted for.

get.summary: List recent audit entries for the org (newest first)
What this node — or this fleet — can actually do
get.description:
Served on BOTH tiers at the same path, and the two answers are different documents: a node reports the one runtime it has, the control plane reports the union across the fleet. The `scope` field ("node" or "fleet") is what tells them apart; branch on it rather than on which URL you called.

`isolation_level` is the vocabulary to ask for a boundary in rather than an engine — see docs/runtimes.md. `strong` means the guest has its own kernel (firecracker); `shared` means a real boundary on a kernel shared with the host (docker); `trusted` means no tenant boundary is claimed (the process runtime, `-tags dev` builds only, never in a release binary). An unrecognised runtime is reported `shared`, never `strong`.

The fleet answer is CAPABILITY, NOT CAPACITY: a level is listed if any node offers it, including nodes that are cordoned, draining or currently full. `nodes.counted` versus `nodes.schedulable` shows that gap. Whether a sandbox can be placed right now is answered by POST /v1/sandboxes, not here.

A node always answers this: describing the boundary it runs code behind is not an optional feature.

503.description: This node has no runtime configured and cannot boot anything. Refused rather than answered, because the document it would otherwise return reports isolation_level "trusted" — an affirmative claim that it runs code with no boundary, where the truth is that it runs nothing.

bearerAuth.description: API key issued from /v1/keys, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'.

Error.description: Every error carries a human-readable message and a stable machine-readable code.

code.description: Stable code: bad_request, unauthorized, payment_required, forbidden, not_found, conflict, payload_too_large, rate_limited, unavailable, error.

template.description: Template id or alias; defaults to the node's first template.

slug.description: Optional DNS label, unique across the platform: the sandbox is served at https://<slug>.<domain>/ (its public port) and every {id} path accepts it. Must start with a lowercase letter; `agent-*` and reserved labels are refused (400); a taken slug is 409 `slug_taken`.

timeout.description: Sandbox TTL in seconds (capped to the plan max).

port.description: App port to publish for the preview URL. On the docker runtime it must be 8000 or a port the template declares, else 400 `port_not_published`.

setup.description: Commands run once after files are written.

start.description: Long-running start command (deploy); its port is published.

slug.description: Present when set; the sandbox is also https://<slug>.<domain>/.

url.description: Preview URL for a published app port.

app_url.description: Preview URL for a deployed start command.

idle_timeout.description: Idle auto-pause in seconds; -1 = never; 0 = platform default.

action.description: e.g. sandbox.create, sandbox.destroy, sandbox.exec, key.create, key.revoke.

TemplateBuild.description: One build of a template. status is 'ready' only once the artifact is durably published and verified; a build in any other status cannot be booted.

rootfs_sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the root filesystem, as carried by the artifact's header.

total_size.description: Bytes across every object of this build.

ready_at.description: Unix seconds; 0 until the build is ready.

ArtifactObject.description: One object of a build that is present in the artifact store.

store_kind.description: Which backend holds the bytes (fs, controlplane).

ok.description: Built, and published where the fleet needs it to be.

log.description: Tail of the build log (last 8000 bytes).

payload.description: What the node produced. `image.tar` is a Docker image tarball, launched with --image <tag>; `rootfs` is a Firecracker template squashfs, launched with --template <template_id>. A client that cannot see which it got cannot use it.

publish.description: Whether the built image reached the shared artifact store, and is therefore obtainable by nodes other than the one that built it.

attempted.description: False when this control plane has no artifact store or no database.

template_id.description: The tag without its version suffix; what a node resolves against.

payload.description: The artifact name the objects were written under, and the same value the artifact's metadata.json carries — so a client reading this response and a node reading the artifact agree without a second lookup.

nodes.description: DEPRECATED. Emitted for one release only, and now always a SINGLE-ELEMENT array describing the one node the build ran on. It used to carry one entry per node in the fleet, because the build was fanned out to all of them; that fan-out was removed (tasks.md section 6.2) and this field describes a mechanism that no longer exists. Read `build` instead. Removed in the release after next.

NodeCapabilities.description: One node's answer: the engine it has and the ceilings it applies.

features.description: Optional command groups this deployment serves, beyond the core sandbox API. Absent on older servers.

runtime.description: Engine name: firecracker, docker or process.

isolation_level.description: The tenant boundary this node provides. See docs/runtimes.md.

isolation.description: The raw capability bit, as sent on this node's heartbeat. True for both firecracker and docker, which is why isolation_level exists.

snapshot.description: Pause frees the sandbox's RAM. False means pause is a SIGSTOP and the memory stays resident.

multiport.description: The preview URL reaches any guest port, not only the declared app port.

auto_pause.description: True when idle sandboxes are paused automatically: the runtime can snapshot and the idle timer is on. On the fleet answer, true only when every counted node pauses. Reported explicitly so a client cannot mistake an absent field for a capability.

templates.description: Template ids this node HOLDS LOCALLY and can boot with no fetch.

templates_enumerated.description: Whether this node enumerates its templates at all. False with an empty `templates` means "boots anything"; TRUE with an empty `templates` means "holds nothing yet". Opposite facts, identical arrays — read this field.

NodeCapabilityLimits.description: The ceilings a create here is held to: the caller's plan, plus this node's own.

max_storage_mb.description: Per-sandbox writable disk. An ENFORCED ceiling: firecracker sizes the sandbox's ext4 overlay from it, and a docker node verifies at boot that its storage driver honours the option, refusing to run in production if it does not.

node_max_active.description: This node's own concurrent-sandbox ceiling, which bounds every org together and is in no plan. The smaller of this and max_concurrent applies.

FleetCapabilities.description: The control plane's answer: the union across the fleet.

features.description: Optional command groups this deployment serves, beyond the core sandbox API. Absent on older servers.

isolation_levels.description: Every level some node offers, STRONGEST FIRST. The order is a ranking and is part of the answer.

runtimes.description: Engine names behind those levels. What to pass as `runtime` on a create to pin placement.

templates.description: Union of what nodes hold locally. A template absent here may still be bootable if can_fetch_templates is true.

can_fetch_templates.description: At least one node has a shared artifact store and can boot a published template nobody holds yet.

FleetNodeCounts.description: The population the capability answer was computed from.

total.description: Every node in the registry, reachable or not.

counted.description: Healthy nodes, which is what the levels above are derived from. Includes cordoned and draining nodes: they still HAVE their isolation.

schedulable.description: How many of those would take a placement right now. Capacity, reported beside the capability rather than mixed into it.
